query: For an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in its uniform, fine lamellar state, whose strength and plasticity remain below industrial application requirements, what single intervention could improve performance for fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive conditions? State the proposed intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome relative to the starting alloy, applicable operating and test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: A tailored thermo‐mechanical processing route—specifically, cryogenic rolling followed by a controlled low‐temperature annealing treatment—will refine and modify the existing uniform fine lamellar microstructure of the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA into a hierarchical dual‐phase microstructure with a higher density of dislocations and finely dispersed, coherent Al‐rich L12 precipitates. This new microstructure is expected to boost yield and tensile strength, enhance ductility and creep resistance, and improve the stability of passive films for better corrosion resistance under extreme thermal fluctuations, long‐term mechanical loading, and corrosive environments.
generation.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in its as-cast, uniform fine lamellar state (with FCC/B2 or L12/B2 phases) that exhibit moderate strength and ductility.
generation.intervention: Single intervention via a combined cryogenic rolling and controlled low-temperature annealing treatment.
generation.conditions: Service conditions including cyclical extreme temperature fluctuations (up to about 700°C), long-term mechanical loading (including sustained stress and room-temperature creep), and exposure to corrosive media such as chloride-containing or molten salt environments.
generation.structural_mediator: A hierarchical dual-phase microstructure characterized by ultrafine grains, enhanced dislocation density, and formation of finely dispersed and coherent Al-rich L12 precipitates along semi-coherent phase boundaries.
generation.mechanism: The cryo-rolling step introduces a high density of lattice defects and refines the existing lamellae while suppressing recovery. The controlled annealing then promotes selective precipitation (e.g., formation of nanoscale Al-rich L12 within the FCC matrix) and recovery without excessive grain coarsening. This combined microstructural evolution enhances dislocation storage, promotes back-stress strengthening, and stabilizes phase interfaces, which together impede creep deformation and restrict pathways for corrosive attack by reinforcing passive film stability.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the starting state, the processed alloy will exhibit significantly higher yield and fracture strengths, improved ductility, and enhanced resistance to creep and corrosive degradation. The refined and stabilized microstructure is expected to sustain these improvements over the extended thermal and mechanical stresses encountered in fastener applications.
generation.baseline: The initial uniform fine lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy, which, although exhibiting a useful balance of strength and ductility, falls short of the stringent performance requirements for fasteners under extreme service conditions.
generation.boundary: Improvements are anticipated under conditions where operating temperatures do not exceed ~700°C, and the corrosive environments (e.g., molten salts or chloride-acid solutions) do not promote rapid microstructural coarsening. The processing benefits must also be maintained over the long-term mechanical loading and cyclic thermal fluctuations typical in fastener service.
generation.uncertainty: While several studies (e.g., PMC6353877::web::018 and PMC5818523::web::002) support that severe plastic deformation plus heat treatments can enhance mechanical performance via hierarchical microstructures, the precise evolution of precipitate stability and interfacial integrity under simultaneously extreme thermal, creep, and corrosion conditions remains to be fully validated.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a set of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy samples in the uniform fine lamellar state. Subject a subset to the proposed cryogenic rolling and controlled annealing treatment while keeping another subset as untreated controls. Develop standardized tests that subject both sets to cyclic thermal fluctuations (e.g., from room temperature to 700°C), long-term mechanical loading including creep tests at room temperature, and corrosion tests in simulated aggressive chloride-containing molten salt or acid environments.
measurements: Tensile and compressive yield strengths; ultimate tensile strength and elongation at room temperature and elevated temperatures.
Creep strain rates under a fixed load at room temperature over an extended period.
Corrosion rates and passive film stability via electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and surface analysis (e.g., XPS, SEM) after exposure.
Microstructural characterization (e.g., TEM and EBSD) to confirm the hierarchical structure and precipitate stability post-processing and post-testing.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the processed alloy does not exhibit statistically significant improvements (for example, comparable or lower yield strength, ductility, creep resistance, or corrosion resistance) relative to the untreated control under the simulated service conditions, or if the beneficial hierarchical microstructure degrades significantly after testing (evidenced by precipitate coarsening or loss of coherent phase boundaries), then the hypothesis will be falsified.
